The `L029 correction <corrections/chiral-residues/v1/PUBLICATION.rst>`_
gives a complete five-page counterexample to Theorem 1.1 in the published
2021 paper On residual connectedness in chiral geometries. Its specified
C-plus group is PSL(2,13), while the full type-preserving group has twice
that order. The full group is chiral, but an actual rank-two residue is
two disjoint six-cycles. All hypotheses of the literal right-coset
construction are verified. Rank-three Proposition 4.11 and a version
requiring chirality under the specified group are not refuted. L029 has
no ordinary recovery, measurement, new-question or Lean credit.

The `L029 correction <../corrections/chiral-residues/v1/PUBLICATION.rst>`_
refutes published Theorem 1.1 using a rank-four chiral coset geometry with
112 objects and 4368 chambers. Full type-preserving Aut has order 2184,
while the specified C-plus group has order 1092. An actual rank-two residue
is two disconnected six-cycles. The rank-three proposition and specified-
group qualification remain separate. This principal refutation adds no
ordinary recovery, measurement, new-question or Lean credit.

L029 has a separate reviewed refutation of Theorem 1.1 in the published
2021 paper \emph{On residual connectedness in chiral geometries}. The
complete five-page proof gives a rank-four geometry with 112 objects and
4368 chambers. The specified group is $\mathrm{PSL}_2(13)$ of order 1092;
its full type-preserving group has order 2184 and two alternating chamber
orbits. An actual rank-two residue is two disconnected six-cycles. Every
hypothesis of the literal right-coset construction is verified. The
rank-three proposition and specified-group variant are not refuted. No
ordinary recovery, measurement, new-question or Lean credit is added.
